text.p: Spanish government bonds closed with gains, cheered by second quarter GDP growth that came in as expected at 1.9 percent year-on-year.

The market kept an eye on the German upward trend and consolidated supports at higher levels. Spanish bonds were a little less fiery than other markets and the differential with the Bund benchmark narrowed slightly.

"The Bund has managed for the most part to surpass highs on the futures and it makes sense there would be a small correction with the differential since we have climbing higher than the others for a good many sessions," one trader said.
Peseta trading was a little thin, although the currency remained firm, as the market weighed the probability the Bank of Spain would cut rates in response to the 1997 budget due Friday.

"No one knows where to go," one currency trader said. "If next week the central bank cuts rates one-quarter point, the peseta and the bonds could continue climbing on the expectation of further cuts."
Dealers said there could be big profit-taking if the cut was a large one.
